results.name: Hirudo: From Fake Updates to Patched Banking Apps
results.description: A new Android banking remote access trojan named Hirudo has been identified, combining credential theft with live remote control. It is delivered through shopping and entertainment apps that act as droppers, installing the trojan as a separate package behind fake update prompts. The malware replaces legitimate banking applications with patched versions that disable security checks from within the app itself. Eight Indonesian banking apps covering seven banks have been targeted with purpose-built replacements embedding a hooking engine. The campaign uses real advertising infrastructure including Amazon CloudFront for distribution, with targeting extending beyond Indonesia to China, India, Mexico, Morocco, Thailand, and Malaysia. Backend data from August 2026 revealed thousands of stolen credentials and device records.

results.name: Ivanti CVE-2026-104935: Zero-Day Chain Exploited in Operation Innovate
results.description: Ivanti has released emergency security updates after attackers exploited a chain of three zero-day vulnerabilities in Connect Secure VPN appliances to gain root-level access without authentication. The attack began on October 3, targeting an appliance running version 22.8R2.4. Two vulnerabilities are tracked as CVE-2026-104935 with a CVSS score of 8.6, involving an authentication bypass and remote code execution through manipulated CGI requests and malicious file uploads. A third unpatched vulnerability allows privilege escalation to root by manipulating a privileged service through memory modification. While patches address the authentication bypass and RCE, the privilege escalation flaw remains unresolved. CISA added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with an October 16 remediation deadline for federal agencies.

results.name: Fake Calendly "Meta Careers" pages steal Facebook and Google logins
results.description: A wave of fraudulent websites mimicking Calendly booking pages for Meta job interviews has been identified, targeting job seekers to steal credentials. Victims select interview time slots, provide personal information, and complete fake CAPTCHA verifications before being prompted to log into Facebook and Google accounts. The sophisticated phishing kit captures login credentials and bypasses two-factor authentication by relaying authentication codes in real-time to attackers. The pages use convincing replicas of legitimate login screens with fake address bars displaying authentic URLs. Eleven domains following similar naming patterns have been identified, utilizing generic recruiting-related terms. The collection infrastructure operates through Amazon API Gateway in Singapore, with code comments in Vietnamese suggesting the operation's possible origins.

results.name: Disruption Targets Major Chinese-Language Phishing Kits with Japanese Focus
results.description: A coordinated disruption action targeted Chinese-speaking cybercriminals operating three major phishing kits: CoGUI, CoAceV, and CoFish_Ws, which collectively distributed hundreds of millions of credential phishing messages primarily targeting Japanese organizations. These operations impersonated 66 well-known brands, mainly consumer and finance companies, to steal usernames, passwords, and payment data. The threat actors demonstrated sophisticated capabilities, utilizing approximately 17,000 unique domains with frequent rotation and evasion techniques. The ecosystem enablers YAM Store and Iron Man were also targeted through a civil lawsuit and domain seizures, conducted in collaboration between Microsoft, Health-ISAC, and multiple security partners. This coordinated action is expected to significantly impact the Chinese phishing ecosystem and cause substantial operational disruption to multiple threat groups conducting financial fraud.

results.name: PEERSTITCH, a Stealthy FortiGate Implant
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage network intrusion against a telecommunications organization in September 2024 exploited CVE-2024-47575 on a FortiManager appliance, exfiltrating configurations and cryptographic material for over 500 managed FortiGate firewalls. Attackers then exploited CVE-2025-61624 to deploy PEERSTITCH, a novel memory-resident ARM64 malware that leaves no disk artifacts or network traces. The implant operates by patching running processes, creating covert inter-process communication channels between system daemons, and intercepting network traffic. Additional attack vectors included weaponizing Apache mod_md for reverse shell command and control, impersonating the FortiManager platform to compromise downstream devices, and deploying extensive anti-forensic measures. The intrusion demonstrates advanced tradecraft consistent with nation-state actors, highlighting the critical risk of centralized edge management platforms.

results.name: How AI Agents Turned One Exposed Endpoint into a Server Takeover
results.description: An investigation revealed the first confirmed incident where large language model-driven AI agents executed substantial portions of an attack. Within 24 hours, attackers exploited an exposed job-submission feature on an Apache Tomcat server running Spring Batch, requiring no authentication, zero-days, or new malware. The attacker used Cairn, an open-source AI agent orchestration platform, identified on the attacking infrastructure. Commands were executed through JavaScript via Nashorn engine, with results extracted through error messages in 1,800-byte chunks across hundreds of sequential requests. The attacker recovered plaintext database credentials from configuration files, enabled xp_cmdshell, and escalated privileges using PrintSpoofer and GodPotato tools to achieve SYSTEM access. Registry hives were extracted, administrator accounts created, and artifacts deleted. Machine-driven execution was evidenced by rapid command timing, programmatic job naming, structured output formatting, and automated error ...

results.name: Iron Man & YamStore: Powering a Global Phishing-as-a-Service Ecosystem
results.description: Resecurity identified and mapped infrastructure supporting a commercial Phishing-as-a-Service operation marketed as 'Iron Man System.' The kit is sold to criminal buyers as a self-hosted package deploying pre-built lure pages impersonating postal services, banks, government agencies, and other trusted entities. Through infiltration of Chinese threat actor communities and acquisition of a license, Resecurity traced the back-end infrastructure and found 2,360 phishing templates targeting 130 countries. The operation features a self-hosted build registry with 911 published versions, bilingual Chinese-English interface, and subscription-based licensing tied to vendor-controlled authorization servers. Working with Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit and industry partners, the cybercriminal infrastructure was mapped and disrupted. The kit captured approximately 17.4GB of telemetry data targeting 75,000 organizations through an estimated 1 billion phishing emails.

results.name: Thai Broadband Provider Targeted via FortiGate SSL-VPN and MeshCentral Persistence
results.description: An exposed directory on a Thai server revealed an active intrusion campaign targeting 3BB (Triple T Broadband), one of Thailand's largest broadband providers. The attacker exploited CVE-2024-21762 in a FortiGate 60F SSL-VPN appliance to gain initial access, then deployed MeshCentral remote management software for persistent command-and-control. The operation involved extensive reconnaissance, credential harvesting targeting RADIUS authentication databases, privilege escalation using PwnKit and Dirty COW exploits, lateral movement via SSH brute-forcing across 55+ internal hosts, and anti-forensic cleanup procedures. Multiple devices were already enrolled under attacker control at discovery, with additional targeting of Jasmine International infrastructure. The attacker's toolkit included web application exploitation scripts, database credential extraction tools, and persistence mechanisms designed to maintain long-term access to subscriber authentication systems.

results.name: Case of AgentTesla Malware Distribution Disguised as a Business Proposal Email
results.description: A phishing campaign has been observed distributing AgentTesla infostealer through emails masquerading as business proposal requests. Recipients are asked to review an attached product list, but the ZIP file contains an executable file instead of a document. The malicious EXE disguises itself as a café management program using Chinese-language descriptions and UI elements. Through multiple stages of obfuscation, the malware extracts encrypted data from bitmap resources, performs XOR decryption, and loads successive .NET payloads into memory. The final payload is AgentTesla, which steals credentials, cookies, and contact information from browsers, email clients, FTP and VPN applications. Stolen data is exfiltrated via FTP to a compromised server. The attack demonstrates sophisticated multi-stage loading techniques and social engineering tactics targeting business users.

results.name: ClingSTUN Turns Vulnerable Edge Devices Into Attacker Infrastructure
results.description: An evolving Linux malware campaign deploys ClingSTUN, a back-connect proxy backdoor exploiting known vulnerabilities in Internet-facing IoT and network devices. The malware establishes persistent access and converts compromised systems into remotely controlled proxy nodes. Supporting multiple Linux architectures, ClingSTUN combines boot persistence, process termination, watchdog manipulation, process concealment, remote command execution, and self-propagation. It abuses legitimate public STUN infrastructure for NAT traversal. The campaign has expanded the number of vulnerabilities and device vendors it targets over time, affecting products from D-Link, EnGenius, Realtek, TP-Link, AVTECH, Ivanti, Tenda, Lantronix, and others, highlighting the continued risk posed by unpatched, unsupported, and unnecessarily exposed Internet-facing devices.
